evidence: Draft judged: “What’s theirs and what’s mine?” against SOURCE.txt (it replaces “What is theirs? What is mine?”; the meaning to keep is his published “What belongs to them?” “What belongs to me?”), CONTEXT.txt and the_change. PRESERVATION: Word by word, “What is” becomes “What’s” (a contraction only); “theirs” and “mine” keep the same two parties in the same order (the other person, then the asker); the only new word is the “and” that joins his two short questions into one. Nothing is added (no claim, condition, person, number, cause or reason), nothing is dropped (this change names no put-back), and strength and who-does-what are unchanged: it still asks the reader to sort what belongs to the other person and what belongs to themself. The one difference is rhythm, one question instead of two beats, which is the point of the swap and not a shift in meaning. The parenthetical in the_change checks out: CONTEXT.txt holds the draft exactly once, and “What boundaries need to be set?” stays as the working copy has it, so the failed first-draft question (“What boundaries do I need to set as a result?”, which dropped his “still” and added a cause) is not in the context. The draft’s apostrophes are curly like the section’s other contractions, and there is no space before the question mark. READS IN CONTEXT: It is the fifth of seven questions, after “What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm?” (so “theirs” points at the other person(s), and C02 is absent) and before “What does accountability require?”; “mine” matches the “I” of the closing question. It reads naturally, and its contraction is no more casual than the section’s “don’t”, “aren’t” and “we’re”. LINTER: B7 short landing at paragraph end is accepted as a false positive here: the linter saw the draft alone, but in the article it sits mid-run, followed by “What does accountability require?” and the longer closing question “How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?”. D9 follows the source order is accepted: it is the generic flag for a passage that tracks its source, and this is a one-sentence swap inside the question run, in the order of the words it replaces, with nothing reordered. I checked T13 and T09 as the flag asks and find both absent: the change adds or removes no reason, aside or callback (the section’s “in a sense” and “It doesn’t make their limitations matter any less” are untouched, so the section keeps its uneven weight), and it joins a pair of three-word questions, so the run is less evenly staccato than before, not more. TELLS: One PRESENT row, T02, at paragraph scale: the closing paragraph is a run of seven compressed questions, each doing one job and handing to the next. I do not accept the writer’s ledger line that the draft is “not part of a run of compressed commands”; it is part of one. I count it justified: it is a list of reflective prompts that the section introduces as questions to ask, and it descends from his published guide (SOURCE.txt cites his “What belongs to them?” “What belongs to me?” and “What boundaries are still needed?” behind the run’s pair and its boundaries question); the change adds no question, and by joining two into one it shortens the run from eight items to seven. Considered and ABSENT: T12 (theirs and mine is a matched pair, but it is the naturally necessary contrast the row exempts, and it is his own pair); T21 (two halves of one job); T20 and T29 (mid-run, not a closer); T06 (its generality is the source’s, and the reader supplies the specifics); T15 (the new words are the more common ones and the structure changed, so there is no less-likely-word swap); T14 (nothing moved or cut); T19 and T25 appear only in the unchanged lead-in sentence and its colon, outside the draft. All other rows (T01, T03 to T05, T07, T08, T10, T11, T16 to T18, T22 to T24, T26 to T28, C01, C03, C04) are absent: a five-word question has no stake, scene, filler, setup, colon, tic word, first-person fact or claim. PROCESS: I formed this view before opening ADMISSION.json and used that file only to check the writer’s claims; I disagree with its ledger on T02 only. My session also carried standing repository instructions that the harness attached (a project CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md text), so “fresh context” in the reviewer origin is slightly less than literal; I opened no file they name and judged only from this brief and the files it names. The only tool use beyond Read and Write was a shell clock read for the turn timestamp, the first made before I opened the brief.
